name: Kang
description: A star 78 parsecs away, 27 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69427: radius 26.674 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 202.724 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.062) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69427: effective temperature 4220 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.031)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69427: distance 78.125 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.02), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 78 parsecs away, 27 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 203 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,220 K, so 26.674 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 69427: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Kappa Virginis
quotes.card: Kappa Virginis, officially named Kang, is a solitary star in the zodiac constellation of Virgo.
quotes.introduction: It has an apparent visual magnitude of 4.18, which is sufficiently bright to be seen with the naked eye.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 6304988355324252928 (quality A), from 2008AJ....135..209M; Gaia DR3 measures none
